intro: ^The first time you saw the girl in the photograph, she was standing beside your grandmother.
^The second time, she was standing alone.
^You discovered the difference three weeks after the funeral. The picture had been hidden between the pages of an old cookbook.
^The photograph was dated June 14th, 1987. Your grandmother was twenty-six. The girl beside her looked exactly like you.

b: ^ The upstairs window in the photograph is open.

call: ^On the back, your grandmother had written: If she comes looking for you, do not tell her your name.
^At that exact moment, the telephone rang.
^“I am calling about the house,” a woman said. “Has anyone opened the upstairs room?”
^Behind her voice, someone was humming a lullaby you remembered from childhood.
room: ^The woman hesitated. “Because it was sealed twenty-nine years ago. And someone opened it last night.”
song: ^The melody stopped. A second voice whispered into the receiver: “She can hear us.”
arrival: ^A cream-coloured envelope. No footsteps followed it. Across the front, in your grandmother’s handwriting: FOR THE ONE WHO STAYED.
^The wax seal showed a small bird surrounded by seven stars.
break: ^Inside, a letter: “There were two of you that summer. But only one came home.”
^A tiny brass key was taped beneath the final line.
light: ^You held the envelope close to the lamp. The paper slowly turned translucent.
^A hidden sentence emerged: “She is not your sister. She is what the house kept.”
^You lowered the letter. The words were gone.
last: ^Three quiet knocks sounded at the window. You lived on the fifth floor.
^The girl in the photograph was no longer looking at your grandmother. She was looking at you.
window: ^Beyond the glass, the night was empty.
^Then a handprint appeared on the outside of the window. Five perfectly ordinary fingers.
^Underneath, a word formed in the condensation: COME.
photo: ^The warning was gone. A new message had appeared in the same handwriting: “You remember me, don’t you?”
^The paper felt warm against your palm.
end: ^By morning, you knew you would return to the house.
^Your grandmother had not been trying to keep you away from it.
^She had been trying to keep something inside.
